dedupe_keys.name: nist o ran testbed automation scripts to deploy 5g open ran testbeds core gnodeb ue ric and xapps

description: The NIST O-RAN Testbed Automation tool deploys and configures 5G Open Radio Access Network testbeds following the blueprints in NIST Technical Note 2311. It sets up, on bare metal or in virtual machines, the 5G core, a gNodeB split into radio unit, distributed unit and centralised unit, user equipment, a RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) and a series of xApps. Coverage: generic laboratory testbeds. The README lists two main scenarios: OCUDU with the O-RAN Software Community Near-RT RIC, and Duranta (OpenAirInterface) with Mosaic5G FlexRIC, plus the O-RAN SC E2 simulator; xApps include KPM monitoring, cell anomaly detection, quality of experience prediction, RIC control and traffic steering, with monitoring output to console, CSV or InfluxDB. Format and access: scripts and documentation on GitHub; free. Licence: NIST software, not subject to copyright in the United States, provided as is (read from the repository licence file). Caveats: minimum system requirements and exact component versions apply; the software was not run for this record. Simulation uses: reproducible 5G and Open RAN testbeds and digital twins to test anomaly detection, traffic steering and resilience of radio access networks. Related records: srsRAN/OCUDU (platform-srsran-ocudu-open-5g-ran) is one of the RAN stacks it deploys, and Colosseum (platform-colosseum-open-ran-digital-twin) is a large Open RAN emulator.
